handoff.summary: Batch b01 curates the four seed factor-accounting identities as scalar definitions/theoretical records: (1) emission mass from activity and factor, (2) CO2-equivalent from gas mass and GWP100, (3) emission intensity per unit output, (4) waste diversion fraction. assumptions: Source assumption: the factor identity applies to the same source, gas, Scope boundary and accounting period with a representative EF matched to the activity (GHGI article; TEAM page: activity data converted with recognised factors).
Application profile: this record formalizes the mass-basis specialization (kg activity x kg/kg factor); energy/volume activity bases require a unit-consistent EF and are separate applications.

gaps: Requires new quantity meanings: emission_mass, activity_amount, emission_factor; new unit kg/kg for the mass-basis factor. Scalar form A*EF fits the engine once meanings/units exist.

models.inverse_notes: E with positive EF determines A = E / EF; E with positive A determines EF = E / A. Original guards apply to the forward direction; each inverse needs its divisor strictly positive (0/0 indeterminate; nonzero/zero has no finite solution). Substitution check: 2500 / 2.5 = 1000 recovers case ordinary-mass-basis; 2500 / 1000 = 2.5 recovers EF. Inversion is algebraic only and does not establish EF transferability across technology, geography or vintage.
limitations: Excludes direct measurement (CEMS), mass-balance/stoichiometric process models, atmospheric fate, dispersion, lifecycle accounting and offset claims.
Does not establish EF representativeness across geography, technology or vintage; a mismatched EF is out of scope and needs its own calibration record.

references.method: Independent elementary multiplication in mass-basis units; 2.5 kg/kg is an illustrative coal-style factor in the Table-1 unit style (kg CO2 per unit fuel mass), not a source-published total.
references.provenance: Independent arithmetic reasoning from stated inputs; not a published measurement.

assumptions: Source assumption: GWP is the IPCC relative energy-absorption index versus 1 kg CO2 over the stated horizon (EPA GWP page; IPCC-TFI FAQ Q1-2-4: ratio of radiative forcing per kg gas to per kg CO2 over a period, currently a 100-year horizon for UNFCCC reporting).
Application profile: this record converts one stated gas at one stated horizon and vintage; multi-gas inventories sum single-gas results with horizon-consistent GWPs.

gaps: Requires new quantity meanings: greenhouse_gas_mass, global_warming_potential, carbon_dioxide_equivalent. Units kg and dimensionless 1 already exist; horizon/vintage carried in context, never interchangeable.

models.inverse_notes: Mco2e with positive GWP determines Mgas = Mco2e / GWP; Mco2e with positive Mgas determines the implied GWP = Mco2e / Mgas. GWP = 0 is only a zero-forcing idealization, not a real gas; CO2 has GWP 1 by definition so converting a CO2 mass is the identity. Substitution checks: 300 / 30 = 10 recovers case ch4-ar6-upper-bound; 546 / 273 = 2 recovers case n2o-ar6. Inversion is algebraic only and does not establish physical equivalence of climate effects.
limitations: Distinguishes the accounting conversion from any physical fate, temperature, damage or offset claim; GWP100 versus GWP20/GTP values are not interchangeable.
Excludes atmospheric physics, decay dynamics, discounting and additionality/offset determinations.

references.method: EPA GWP page reports methane GWP100 as 27-30 (Sixth Assessment, 100-year); 30 used as the stated published bound; expected is independent multiplication 10 x 30.
references.provenance: Published factor bound combined with independent multiplication; the 300 total is derived, not source-published.

references.method: EPA GWP page states nitrous oxide has a GWP 273 times CO2 for a 100-year timescale (Sixth Assessment); expected is independent multiplication 2 x 273.

models.inverse_notes: I with positive Q determines E = I x Q; I with positive E determines Q = E / I. Q = 0 is excluded by the guard (per-unit intensity undefined); I = 0 with positive Q implies zero emissions; 0/0 is indeterminate. Substitution checks: 0.1 x 100000 = 10000 recovers case bakery-a; 10000 / 0.1 = 100000 recovers Q. Inversion is algebraic only and does not establish causal or efficiency claims.
limitations: A falling intensity alongside rising absolute emissions still increases atmospheric loading; intensity does not measure climate impact, fate or offsets.
Denominator choice shapes the story (revenue versus physical output); cross-company comparison requires the same metric and boundary.

references.provenance: Value derived from a published illustration after a documented unit conversion; arithmetic independently checked.

models.inverse_notes: D with positive Mt determines Md = D x Mt; D with positive Md determines Mt = Md / D (needs D > 0); D = 0 with any positive Mt implies Md = 0 while Mt stays underdetermined. Substitution checks: 0.3214774282 x 292.4 ~= 94 recovers case epa-2018-national; 94 / 0.3214774282 ~= 292.4 recovers Mt. Inversion is algebraic only and does not establish stream eligibility or facility performance.
limitations: A mass-based diversion rate is not a greenhouse-gas inventory; waste mass is activity data requiring separate factors, method and boundary for any Scope 3 estimate.
Stream definitions change comparability: EPA excludes 17.7 Mt of other food management and 34.6 Mt combusted with energy recovery from the 32.1% headline rate.

references.method: EPA National Overview publishes 69 Mt recycled + 25 Mt composted (about 94 Mt) of 292.4 Mt generated as a 32.1% headline rate; expected is the independently computed fraction 94/292.4 (headline is the rounded percent).
references.provenance: Values derived from published EPA figures; the fraction is independently computed, not source-published as a fraction.
